record.original_question: Determine the weight enumerator of the self-dual binary Reed–Muller code R_2(4,9), which the chapter identifies as the remaining unknown Reed–Muller weight enumerator at length 512.

evidence.quote: Since the dual of R2(3, 9) is R2(5, 9), only the weight enumerator of R2(4, 9), the self-dual code, remains unknown.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For nonnegative integers $r \le m$, the binary Reed–Muller code $R(r,m)$ of length $2^m$ is the linear code over $\mathbb{F}_2$ whose codewords are the evaluation vectors $(f(x))_{x \in \mathbb{F}_2^m}$ of all Boolean polynomials $f \in \mathbb{F}_2[x_1,\dots,x_m]$ of degree at most $r$. The dual code of $R(r,m)$ is $R(m-r-1,m)$; in particular, $R(4,9)$ is a doubly-even self-dual binary code of length $512$ and dimension $256$.

Determine the complete weight distribution of $R(4,9)$: that is, compute the integer $A_w := \#\{c \in R(4,9) : \mathrm{wt}(c) = w\}$ for every $w \in \{0,1,2,\dots,512\}$, where $\mathrm{wt}(c)$ denotes the Hamming weight, and hence the weight enumerator $W(x,y) = \sum_{w=0}^{512} A_w\, x^{512-w} y^{w}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The weight distribution of R(4,9) has been determined. A 2023/2024 preprint by Carlet and an independent computation, followed by a 2025 paper "The weight distribution of the fourth-order Reed–Muller code of length 512" in Designs, Codes and Cryptography, report the full weight spectrum, completing the table of Reed–Muller weight enumerators at length 512.

status_evidence.title: The weight distribution of the fourth-order Reed–Muller code of length 512
status_evidence.snippet: The weight spectrum of the fourth order Reed–Muller code R(4,9) of length 512 has been found and presented.
status_evidence.claim: The weight distribution of R(4,9) has been computed.

status_evidence.title: Weight Distribution of the Binary Reed-Muller Code R(4,9) (preprint)
status_evidence.snippet: Computing the Weight Distribution of the Binary Reed-Muller Code R(4,9), using classification of Boolean quartic forms and affine equivalence classes.
status_evidence.claim: An explicit computation of the weight distribution of R(4,9) has been carried out.
